1.modern-en: Antony appears at Cleopatra's palace dismissing the news from Rome and declaring that the empire is well lost for her.

2.modern-en: Antony hears the soothsayer's warnings against him in Cleopatra's antechamber.

3.modern-en: Antony takes leave of Cleopatra after the news of Fulvia's death and the trouble with Caesar.

4.modern-en: Antony is mentioned in absentia in Caesar's complaints to Lepidus about his idleness in Egypt.

5.modern-en: Antony arrives in Rome to face Caesar and the political reckoning.

6.modern-en: Antony confronts Caesar about Fulvia's wars and the unpaid alliance.

7.modern-en: Antony accepts the political marriage to Octavia and embraces Caesar.

11.modern-en: Antony, with Caesar and Lepidus, dines aboard Pompey's galley and lets himself get drunk with the rest.

12.modern-en: Antony is mentioned in Cleopatra's furious quarrel with the messenger about Octavia.

13.modern-en: Antony bids Octavia farewell as she leaves to mediate between him and Caesar.

15.modern-en: Antony slips back to Cleopatra in the east and is at her court when Caesar's army moves.

16.modern-en: Antony's quarrel with Caesar reaches breaking point; preparations for war begin.

17.modern-en: Antony decides, over Enobarbus's protest, to fight Caesar at sea at Actium.

24.modern-en: Antony commands at Actium and follows Cleopatra's fleeing ship out of the battle.

25.modern-en: Antony refuses to look at Cleopatra after the defeat, then forgives her.

26.modern-en: Antony sends his old schoolmaster as ambassador to Caesar, asking only to live as a private man in Egypt.

27.modern-en: Antony catches Caesar's messenger kissing Cleopatra's hand and has him whipped.

28.modern-en: Antony orders a feast and a final assault: 'one other gaudy night.'

29.modern-en: Antony bids his servants farewell in their last evening together.

30.modern-en: Antony hears strange music under the stage as if Hercules, his patron, abandons him.

31.modern-en: Antony arms for battle and is helped into his harness by Cleopatra and Eros.

32.modern-en: Antony wins his last land battle, returns triumphant to Cleopatra, and is kissed by her in front of the army.

33.modern-en: Antony, betrayed by the fleet at the second sea-fight, rages at Cleopatra and threatens her life.

34.modern-en: Antony, deceived by a report that Cleopatra has killed herself, tries to fall on his sword and only half-succeeds.

35.modern-en: Antony is borne up into Cleopatra's monument on ropes and dies kissing her.

1.modern-en: Cleopatra opens the play teasing Antony in her palace and refusing to let him attend to Rome.

3.modern-en: Cleopatra throws a hundred jealous tantrums between dawn and noon over the messenger from Rome.

5.modern-en: Cleopatra languishes in Antony's absence, sends messengers after him, and pines aloud.

8.modern-en: Cleopatra plays with her women and remembers Antony fishing for her on the Nile.

12.modern-en: Cleopatra beats and threatens the messenger who brings the news of Antony's marriage to Octavia.

15.modern-en: Cleopatra grills the returning messenger about Octavia's looks and height, mollified only by the report that Octavia is short.

16.modern-en: Cleopatra prepares for war alongside Antony, refusing to be left out of the fleet.

17.modern-en: Cleopatra insists on commanding her own ships at Actium.

21.modern-en: Cleopatra and her women observe the gathering Roman forces and the omens against them.

23.modern-en: Cleopatra panics at Actium, turns her flagship away, and Antony's fleet follows.

25.modern-en: Cleopatra begs Antony's forgiveness after the defeat and is given it.

26.modern-en: Cleopatra hears Antony's terms to Caesar and adds, secretly, her own.

28.modern-en: Cleopatra joins Antony's defiant feast and toasts the final assault.

30.modern-en: Cleopatra dresses Antony for battle, mocking his armour into place.

31.modern-en: Cleopatra welcomes Antony back from the first day's victory and crowns him with kisses.

32.modern-en: Cleopatra cowers from Antony's rage after the fleet betrays him and flees to her monument.

33.modern-en: Cleopatra sends Mardian to tell Antony she has killed herself, then has the door barred.

34.modern-en: Cleopatra hauls the dying Antony up to her monument and listens to his last advice.

36.modern-en: Cleopatra is captured in her monument by Proculeius and meets Caesar's emissary.

37.modern-en: Cleopatra plays the broken queen for Caesar himself, refusing him nothing in words and granting nothing in fact.

38.modern-en: Cleopatra has Iras and Charmian help her dress in her royal robes for the end.

39.modern-en: Cleopatra receives the clown with the figs and the asps and prepares to die.

40.modern-en: Cleopatra puts an asp to her breast and one to her arm and dies upright in her chair.

41.modern-en: Cleopatra is found by Caesar's men, dead, with Iras at her feet and Charmian arranging her crown.

42.modern-en: Cleopatra is ordered by Caesar to be buried with Antony in royal state.

epithet.en: Triumvir of Rome, the future Augustus

4.modern-en: Caesar complains to Lepidus about Antony's life in Egypt and reads aloud the report on his behaviour.

7.modern-en: Caesar receives Antony in Rome and arranges the political marriage to Octavia.

11.modern-en: Caesar dines aboard Pompey's galley but refuses to get drunk.

14.modern-en: Caesar welcomes Octavia back to Rome without the proper escort she had every right to expect.

17.modern-en: Caesar moves his forces east as the war with Antony becomes inevitable.

22.modern-en: Caesar prepares the fleet for Actium.

26.modern-en: Caesar receives the schoolmaster Antony sends as ambassador and rejects the terms.

27.modern-en: Caesar sends Thidias to Cleopatra to detach her from Antony.

32.modern-en: Caesar is briefly checked by Antony's land victory.

35.modern-en: Caesar hears the news of Antony's death and weeps for him in front of his commanders.

37.modern-en: Caesar visits Cleopatra in the monument, plays the kindly conqueror, and intends to lead her in triumph.

38.modern-en: Caesar sends Dolabella to her with reassurances about her treatment.

39.modern-en: Caesar's officer Dolabella warns Cleopatra that she will be paraded through Rome within three days.

42.modern-en: Caesar orders the joint burial of Antony and Cleopatra, the war over and the empire effectively his.

epithet.en: Antony's closest friend and most loyal officer

2.modern-en: Enobarbus is at Cleopatra's court trading wit with her women and warning Antony to attend to Rome.

5.modern-en: Enobarbus accompanies Antony back to Rome.

7.modern-en: Enobarbus delivers his great speech on Cleopatra's barge ('The barge she sat in, like a burnished throne') to Maecenas and Agrippa.

9.modern-en: Enobarbus is on Pompey's galley and trades drinks with the other commanders.

11.modern-en: Enobarbus is at the feast aboard the galley and laughs about Lepidus passing out.

15.modern-en: Enobarbus argues against fighting at sea at Actium and is overruled.

18.modern-en: Enobarbus is at the muster of Antony's land forces.

20.modern-en: Enobarbus debates desertion with himself after Actium.

23.modern-en: Enobarbus follows Antony out of Actium with a heavy heart.

25.modern-en: Enobarbus watches Antony's recovery from despair and tells the audience he has decided to leave him.

27.modern-en: Enobarbus, having deserted to Caesar, learns that Antony has sent his treasure after him.

28.modern-en: Enobarbus, sick with shame, withdraws to a ditch outside Caesar's camp.

30.modern-en: Enobarbus dies of grief in the trench, calling Antony's name as he goes.

7.modern-en: Octavia is given by Caesar to Antony as a wife to seal the alliance, and meets her new husband for the first time on stage.

13.modern-en: Octavia takes leave of Antony to try to mediate between her husband and her brother.

14.modern-en: Octavia arrives back in Rome with only a small escort and is met by a cold Caesar who tells her that Antony is back with Cleopatra.

1.modern-en: Charmian is with Cleopatra at the play's opening, teasing the soothsayer about her fortune.

3.modern-en: Charmian helps Cleopatra play her moods through Antony's day of departure.

5.modern-en: Charmian attends Cleopatra through her sulking absence.

8.modern-en: Charmian shares her queen's memories of Antony fishing for her on the Nile.

12.modern-en: Charmian holds Cleopatra back from killing the messenger who brings news of Octavia.

30.modern-en: Charmian helps Cleopatra dress Antony for battle.

33.modern-en: Charmian advises Cleopatra to send the fake report of her death to Antony.

36.modern-en: Charmian helps Cleopatra bar herself into the monument.

39.modern-en: Charmian dresses her queen in royal robes for the end.

40.modern-en: Charmian dies a moment after Cleopatra, with the asp at her arm, arranging the crown on her dead mistress's head.

epithet.en: Pompey the Great's son, a Roman rebel

4.modern-en: Pompey is mentioned in Caesar's councils as the next great problem, rising in Sicily and Sardinia.

7.modern-en: Pompey is at sea raiding Roman shipping while the triumvirs assemble against him.

10.modern-en: Pompey negotiates terms with the triumvirs at Misenum and accepts a peace.

11.modern-en: Pompey hosts the triumvirs aboard his galley and refuses Menas's offer to murder them while they are drunk.

epithet.en: The third triumvir, soon to be sidelined

4.modern-en: Lepidus tries to keep Caesar talking calmly about Antony.

7.modern-en: Lepidus mediates the public reconciliation of Caesar and Antony.

10.modern-en: Lepidus is at the Misenum conference with Pompey.

11.modern-en: Lepidus is carried off Pompey's galley too drunk to stand, the joke of the evening.

epithet.en: Antony's freedman, his most personal servant

20.modern-en: Eros is at Antony's side after Actium, helping him keep up some appearance of command.

29.modern-en: Eros joins the farewell dinner with Antony's servants.

31.modern-en: Eros arms Antony before the last day's battle.

34.modern-en: Eros, ordered by Antony to kill him, kills himself instead rather than strike his master.
